name: Antigua and Barbuda

facts.religion: Christian, mostly Anglican and other Protestant

snapshot: A twin-island Caribbean state built on tourism, led by Gaston Browne, who is pushing for reparations for slavery and has floated becoming a republic.
culture: Antigua claims a beach for every day of the year. Carnival, held in late July and early August to mark emancipation from slavery in 1834, is the biggest event of the year, with calypso and steel pan competitions. Cricket is a passion; Sir Viv Richards, one of the game's greatest batsmen, is Antiguan, and the national stadium bears his name.
society: Tourism, especially cruise ships and luxury resorts, accounts for most of the economy. Barbuda, the sister island, was devastated by Hurricane Irma in 2017, and a dispute over land rights there has pitted Barbudans against the government. A citizenship-by-investment programme is a big source of revenue.
baseline: Gaston Browne's Antigua and Barbuda Labour Party won a third term in 2023 with a reduced majority. Browne has been a prominent voice for climate finance and slavery reparations, and has said a referendum on becoming a republic could follow.

leaders.state: King Charles III, represented by a governor-general
